Census and the 2026 vote, by ward

How to use this tool
  • Choose an election outcome to plot on the vertical axis.
  • Choose a census year and a census variable for the horizontal axis. Census 2011 offers more variables; Census 2022 is more recent but covers only population group, age, sex and density, and its figures are modelled estimates.
  • Choose a straight-line (linear) or smoothed (loess) fit, and all wards or a single province.
  • Hover over (or tap) a point to see its ward and values.
  • The sentence above the plot provides interpretation based on the regression estimate shown below the plot.
How to read the results
  • Each point is a 2026 ward.
  • The slope is the expected difference in the outcome for a ward one unit higher on the census variable (e.g. one percentage point), from an ordinary least squares regression with each ward counted once. Its confidence interval allows for wards in the same municipality being alike (standard errors clustered by municipality).
  • These are associations across wards, not effects on individual voters.
Sources: Electoral Commission of South Africa (election returns), Statistics South Africa (Census 2011, Census 2022), Municipal Demarcation Board (ward boundaries).
